plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional diagram of the torque produced by a force acting at a point away from the origin. Thin black axes labeled x toward the lower left, y to the right, and z upward meet at a point marked O. A heavy blue arrow labeled r, with an overhead vector arrow, runs from O down and to the right to a black dot labeled P. At P a red arrow labeled F points to the right and slightly upward, and a dashed line extends the line of r past P; the angle between that dashed extension and F is marked theta, with the same angle theta repeated on the far side of F where the dashed line of action continues to the lower right. A thin segment from near the origin meets that dashed line at a small right-angle square and is labeled r_perp. An orange arrow labeled tau rises straight up from P, standing perpendicular to the plane that holds r and F. Below and to the left, a drawn open right hand repeats the same blue r and red F arrows with curved black arrows wrapping around them to indicate the sense in which the fingers curl. Showing the geometric construction and the hand together supplies both the magnitude of the cross product, fixed by r, F, and theta, and its direction, which here lies along the positive z-axis.

elements: origin point marked O
x-axis pointing toward the lower left, thin black line
y-axis pointing to the right, thin black line
z-axis pointing straight up, thin black line
thick blue vector arrow r from O down and to the right to point P
black dot marking point P at the tip of r
red vector arrow F originating at P, pointing right and slightly upward in the r–F plane
orange vector arrow tau rising vertically from P (along +z), with length proportional to |r||F|sin(theta)
dashed black line extending r past P (line of action reference) in both directions
thin black segment r_perp from near O meeting the dashed line at a small right-angle square marker
theta angle arc between the dashed extension of r and F at P
second theta arc on the far side of F where the dashed line of action continues lower right
vector labels: r, F, tau, r_perp, theta, O, P
right-hand-rule overlay (toggle): drawn open right hand below-left of the axes with miniature blue r and red F arrows emerging from it and curved black arrows showing finger curl toward tau

interactions.label: Angle θ between r and F
interactions.teaches: Rotating F about P changes only the sin(θ) factor: the tau arrow grows to maximum length near 90° and nearly vanishes when r and F align, showing |τ| = rF sin θ

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching to the hand overlay connects the sin θ magnitude construction to direction: curled fingers follow F rotating toward r and the thumb points along tau (+z), making the cross-product direction rule explicit
Rotating the scene reveals that r and F lie in a plane and tau stands perpendicular to that plane along +z

demo_steps.title: Aligned force, weak torque
demo_steps.narration: With θ = 20°, F is nearly parallel to r: r_perp is short and the orange tau arrow almost vanishes — a force through the pivot cannot twist it.

demo_steps.title: Perpendicular force, maximum torque
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 90° the moment arm r_perp equals the full r, and tau reaches its maximum length — the entire force contributes to rotation.

demo_steps.title: Right-hand rule
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the hand cue: the fingers curl from r toward F and the thumb points up along tau, giving the torque direction along +z for this configuration.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Origin O at (0,0,0). Axes span ±3 units, thin black; +x toward lower-left of screen, +y right, +z up. r vector: thick blue (#1a3a6b) arrow from O to P at approximately (1.6, 2.2, 0) — pointing down-right in screen space as in the source; r lies in the x–y plane (z=0). F: red (#cc2200) arrow from P, rotated in the z=0 plane by angle θ measured from the dashed forward extension of r (source shows θ ≈ 30–40°, F pointing right and slightly up); |F| ≈ 1.4 units. tau: orange (#ee7b0d) arrow from P along +z, length = rF·sin(θ) scaled so τ = rF at θ=90° gives ~1.8 units. Dashed black line through P along r's direction, extending ~1 unit past P each way; r_perp thin black segment from O perpendicular to that line with a small right-angle square; both θ arcs rendered as small angle markers at P. Layout matches source: axes upper-left, vectors center-right, hand overlay lower-left. In right-hand-rule mode, dim r_perp and the θ arcs, show the hand with curled-finger arrows around the r/F junction and highlight tau.
interactionPlan.notes: Recompute F's direction, r_perp segment, both θ arcs, and tau's length reactively on every slider change; keep r fixed. Render vectors with CylinderGeometry+ConeGeometry arrowheads for thickness matching the source. The hand can be a stylized simplified mesh or a textured sprite plane — it must include the two curved arrows indicating curl sense. Arc labels (θ) should billboard toward the camera.

authoredContext:
When a force F→ is applied to a point P whose position is r→ relative to O (the figure), the torque τ→ around O is

The cross product r→×F→ also tells us the sign of the torque. In the figure, the cross product r→×F→ is along the positive z-axis, which by convention is a positive torque. If r→×F→ is along the negative z-axis, this produces a negative torque.

Now let’s consider how to define torques in the general three-dimensional case.

The torque is perpendicular to the plane defined by r→andF→ and its direction is determined by the right-hand rule.

Figure shows an XYZ coordinate system. Force F is applied in the XY plane and is parallel to the X axis. Vector r lies in the XY plane. It starts at the origin of the origin of the coordinate system and ends at the beginning of vector F. Vector for torque starts at the intersection point of r and v vectors. It is perpendicular to the XY plane and is pointed into the Z direction.

demo_steps.narration: With θ = 20°, F is nearly parallel to r: r_perp is short and the orange tau arrow almost vanishes — a force through the pivot cannot twist it.

demo_steps.title: Perpendicular force, maximum torque
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 90° the moment arm r_perp equals the full r, and tau reaches its maximum length — the entire force contributes to rotation.

demo_steps.title: Right-hand rule
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the hand cue: the fingers curl from r toward F and the thumb points up along tau, giving the torque direction along +z for this configuration.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional diagram of the torque produced by a force acting at a point away from the origin. Thin black axes labeled x toward the lower left, y to the right, and z upward meet at a point marked O. A heavy blue arrow labeled r, with an overhead vector arrow, runs from O down and to the right to a black dot labeled P. At P a red arrow labeled F points to the right and slightly upward, and a dashed line extends the line of r past P; the angle between that dashed extension and F is marked theta, with the same angle theta repeated on the far side of F where the dashed line of action continues to the lower right. A thin segment from near the origin meets that dashed line at a small right-angle square and is labeled r_perp. An orange arrow labeled tau rises straight up from P, standing perpendicular to the plane that holds r and F. Below and to the left, a drawn open right hand repeats the same blue r and red F arrows with curved black arrows wrapping around them to indicate the sense in which the fingers curl. Showing the geometric construction and the hand together supplies both the magnitude of the cross product, fixed by r, F, and theta, and its direction, which here lies along the positive z-axis.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for angle theta between r and F: learner rotates the force direction about point P; r_perp and the tau arrow length grow to a maximum near 90 degrees and shrink near alignment; the dependence of torque magnitude on sin(theta) becomes visible.
- Toggle between geometric construction and right-hand-rule overlay: learner switches from the r_perp/angle diagram to the hand cue; the curl direction and resulting tau arrow highlight together; the rule connecting rotation sense to torque direction becomes clear.
